newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 28.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- NOTTINGHAM FOREST SETS DEADLINE FOR BIDS

Premiership football club Nottingham Forest has set a Friday deadline for all offers for control of the club. The club has sent out notices to convene a special shareholder's meeting for February 24. The only formal offer currently being considered is a 15 million stg offer from Nigel Wray, the millionaire owner of rugby union club Saracens. He is financing a bid by former Tottenham chairman Irving Scholar and Philip Soar.
-- ROLLS-ROYCE LANDS 300 MILLION STG EMIRATES DEAL

Dubai-based airline Emirates has become the only carrier in the world to have its entire fleet powered by Rolls-Royce aero- engines after placing an order worth $500 million. The airline has ordered Trent 700 engines for Airbus A330 aircraft to provide Rolls-Royce with a clean sweep and take business placed with British aerospace companies above the $1 billion mark. Emirates has spent the last six months evaluating the merits of Rolls-Royce engines and rival products from GE and Pratt & Whitney, the American aero-engine manufacturers.
-- SKIPTON PUTS 2,000 STG MINIMUM ON BALANCES

Skipton Building Society have announced that accounts where balances fall below 2,000 stg will be closed automatically. Speculation that the society might seek a stock market float or takeover, leading to windfall bonuses for members, has spurred an increase in applications for new accounts. Skipton, the 13th largest society, will become eighth in the league table after building society conversions in the summer.
THE TIMES
-- RAILTRACK TARGETS LONDON TUBE FOR TAKEOVER

Railtrack chairman Sir Robert Horton is planning a takeover bid for London Underground if the tube's track and signalling is privatised as a separate infrastructure company. He believes that huge benefits for passengers could be achieved by combining the underground and main-line networks under single ownership. He told ministers that only a company with the size and expertise of Railtrack could pay the one billion stg backlog of investment need to modernise the system.
-- PRU FINED 75,000 STG OVER PEP BREACHES

Prudential, Britain's largest life and pensions company with 85 billion stg under management, has been fined by Imro, the City watchdog, 75,000 stg for a series of breaches of rules in its Personal Equity Plan division. Imro also announced that Prudential had paid 25,000 stg in compensation to 6,000 disadvantaged investors and had been ordered by an independent disciplinary tribunal to pay Imro's costs.
-- CLARKE EXPECTED TO HOLD RATES LINE AT NEXT GEORGE MEETING

The City believes that base rates will be left on hold in next month's monetary meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and the governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, due to steady but unspectacular economic growth in the final quarter of last year. Figures from the Office of National Statistics show that gross domestic product expanded 0.8 percent in the final three months of 1996, slightly stronger than the 0.7 percent recorded in the third quarter.
THE GUARDIAN
-- TWO TORY FUND-RAISERS DRAWN INTO CANTORS SHARE PROBE

Lord Harris of Peckham and Sir Graham Kirkham, two top fund-raisers for the Conservative Party, are part of a share- dealing investigation by the DTI. The DTI is focusing on share trading in a Sheffield-based furniture company, Cantors, ahead of its merger last year with Harveys, a private company owned by Lord Harris. Lord Graham heads the DFS Furniture stores chain. There is no suggestion that either fundraisers are involved in the share trading at the centre of the inquiry.
-- 'WHITE KNIGHT' ENTERS NEWMAN FRAY

Ingersoll-Rand, the US components group, have emerged with a 230 million stg "white knight" counter-bid for the building materials group Newman Tonks. Newman has been fighting a 196 million stg cash-and-shares bid from engineering conglomerate FKI. The company said it was recommending the all-cash counter- bid. However, speculation has increased that FKI is poised to raise its offer.
-- UNION JOINS COMPANY CHIEFS IN CALL FOR FOREIGN INVESTMENT

The Amalgamated Engineering and Electrical Union has published a joint appeal with industrialists, such as chief executive of British Airways, Bob Ayling, and directors of Bosch, Toyota, Sharp, Vauxhall, Nissan and Electrolux, to Far Eastern and German firms to invest in Britain. The Union is committed to deliver profitability and efficiency to shareholders. The AEEU's brochure is very similar to the Government's view that Britain is a high-skill, low-strike manufacturing investment base.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- STAGECOACH HELD UP BY THREAT OF MMC REFERRAL

Bus and train group Stagecoach, has been warned by the Government that it could be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission if it was selected to run ScotRail, operator of rail services in Scotland. Corporate and consumer affairs minister John Taylor took the decision after being advised by John Bridgeman, the Director General of Fair Trading, that a takeover would lead to competition concerns in Scotland.
-- STEEL SELLS BSF FOR 74.5 MILLION STG IN STRATEGIC U-TURN

British Steel have announced a strategic U-turn with a 74.5 million stg deal to sell off British Steel Forgings, its forging business, which makes a wide range of products for the engineering industry. This comes just two years after British Steel bought out the car parts group GKN, its partner in the division, arguing that the engineering steel business was now a "core activity".
-- HOUSE OF FRASER WARNS MORE JOBS ARE IN DANGER

Department store group, House of Fraser is set to sell three stores and cut 1,000 jobs in an overhaul that will result in the group taking a 50 million stg charge against this year's accounts. The provisions include heavy stock write-offs and will push House of Fraser into the red this year. Chief executive John Coleman said there would be no more store sales but would not rule out any further job losses.
